head: A clothing star
started selling carrots.
slides.sub: And quit within about two years.

image.label: A fleece jacket beside a crate of vegetables
image.brief: 플리스 재킷 옆에 놓인 채소 상자. 단정한 일본 매장 조명.

head: Uniqlo could
do no wrong.
body: By the early 2000s, Uniqlo's fleece craze had made its parent, Fast Retailing, one of Japan's most admired companies.
Founder Tadashi Yanai was looking for the next big business.

image.label: Shoppers lining up outside a Tokyo clothing store
image.brief: 도쿄 의류 매장 앞에 늘어선 쇼핑객 행렬. 로고 없음.

head: Same model,
new product.
body: In 2002, a Fast Retailing company launched SKIP, a brand of fresh vegetables and fruit sold to households in the Tokyo area.
The plan was to bring Uniqlo's methods to food: control from farm to customer, good quality, fair prices.

image.label: Fresh produce in neat branded boxes

head: It works for clothes.
Will it work for food?
body: You have mastered planning, sourcing and selling at scale. Vegetables are a huge market.

options.text: Launch and scale fast, the way Uniqlo did
options.feedback: Speed won in clothing. Keep swiping.

options.text: Test small with a few farms and customers first
options.feedback: Slower, but much cheaper to be wrong. Keep swiping.

options.text: Stay out: it is not your business
options.feedback: It means passing on growth. Keep swiping.

image.label: A fork in a farm road

head: Clothes can wait.
Vegetables can't.
body: A fleece can sit in a warehouse for weeks. Spinach can't. Weather changes harvests, quality varies box by box, and every day of delay ruins stock.

head: The supermarket
was still easier.
body: Shoppers already had supermarkets nearby with fresh produce every day. The new service struggled to win enough steady customers to cover its costs.

image.label: A supermarket produce aisle full of shoppers
image.brief: 손님으로 붐비는 동네 슈퍼마켓 채소 코너.

slides.label: the year Fast Retailing pulled out of the vegetable business
body: The venture closed with losses. In his 2003 book, One Win, Nine Losses, Yanai had already argued that failures are part of how a company grows.

head: Back to
clothes.
body: Fast Retailing refocused on apparel and on taking Uniqlo abroad. It went on to become one of the world's largest clothing retailers.

image.label: Racks of clothing in a busy overseas store
image.brief: 해외 대형 매장의 의류 진열대. 로고 없음.

head: Your strengths fit
your old business.
body: Uniqlo's edge came from controlling every step of making and selling clothes. Food works differently: it spoils, varies and depends on the weather.
Moving into a new market is a bet that your strengths still apply there. Sometimes they don't.

image.label: A key that fits one lock but not another
image.brief: 한 자물쇠에는 맞고 다른 자물쇠에는 맞지 않는 열쇠.

head: Check how the market
works before you jump.
body: A winning formula only travels if the new market works the same way underneath.
**Try it today:** list the three things that make your business good. Would all three still hold in your next market?

image.label: A single carrot on a clothing shelf
image.brief: 옷 진열대 위에 놓인 당근 하나.

factChecks.note: Fast Retailing 자회사 FR Foods의 SKIP 브랜드 출범(2002년 가을)과 판매 방식(회원제·택배와 일부 매장)은 Fast Retailing 공시와 당시 보도로 확인하세요. 카드에는 "sold to households in the Tokyo area"로만 적었습니다.
철수 시점(2004년)과 손실 규모는 Fast Retailing 공시로 확인하세요. 손실 금액은 넣지 않았습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] SKIP 매장 4월 말 폐점, FR Foods 6월 청산(2004년), 2003년 6월 결산 매출 6억 5천만 엔·손실 9억 3천만 엔, 특별손실 28억 엔 확인(Retail Week).
야나이 다다시의 책 「一勝九敗」(2003, 신초샤)의 영어 제목은 비공식 번역입니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 『一勝九敗』 2003년 신초샤 출간 확인.
실패 원인(신선도 관리, 품질 편차, 고객 확보)은 당시 보도와 회사 설명을 일반화한 것입니다. 원문 보도로 표현을 확인하세요.
Fast Retailing이 세계 최대급 의류 소매기업이 되었다는 표현은 매출 순위 자료로 확인하세요.
